prompt:
Repair solution.mjs for a synthetic revisable activity-session aggregator. Late bridges should merge open sessions, retracting a bridge should split them, and finalized sessions must remain stable. Reusing fixed epoch-window rules has produced wrong membership and lateness decisions. Do not access a broker or live service.

Export sessions({gap_ms,lateness_ms,records}). gap_ms>0 and lateness_ms>=0 are integers. Records, in receipt order, are upsert {kind,id,rev,key,event_time,amount}, delete {kind,id,rev}, or watermark {kind,time}. IDs/keys are ASCII strings, rev positive integer, times signed integer milliseconds, amounts signed integers including0. At most80 records and18 logical IDs. Only greatest accepted revisions establish current state. Lower revisions do nothing; repeating an accepted revision with the same canonical payload does nothing; changed payload at that accepted revision throws an Error. A delete of an unknown ID is a valid revision tombstone. A rejected change establishes neither revision nor payload. All inputs are well formed.

For each key, current live events are sorted by event_time. A session is a maximal connected component whose consecutive event times differ by <=gap_ms (equality connects). Its start is first event_time and its end is last event_time+gap_ms. Its count is logical event count, total is their sum, and ids are ASCII-sorted. Equal-content distinct IDs are distinct events. These are sessions, not fixed epoch buckets.

Watermark begins null and advances monotonically to the maximum explicit watermark record; it is not inferred from events. A current session becomes permanently finalized when its end<=watermark-lateness_ms. Finalization is applied after each accepted change as well as watermark advancement, so a retraction can split an open session and leave an older resulting component finalized. Finalized membership, times and values cannot change.

A greater-revision delete/upsert of an event already in a finalized session is rejected atomically. A new/upsert event is also rejected if its proposed time lies within gap_ms of any finalized session of that key (including equality to its boundary); it must not join or extend that sealed component. For other upserts, evaluate the session containing the proposed event under the complete proposal, including removal of its old contribution: that resulting session must have end>watermark-lateness_ms if a watermark exists. An individually old event can therefore be accepted when it joins an open session whose resulting end remains open. Rejecting a move leaves its old contribution and version intact. A delete of an unsealed/unknown event is allowed; resulting open components are regrouped and may finalize. Exact accepted-revision replay/conflict and lower-revision rules apply even after finalization.

Return exactly {watermark,sessions}, sorted by numeric start then key. Each session has exactly {key,start,end,total,count,ids,final}; final is boolean. Keep nonempty zero-total sessions. With no watermark no session is final. Empty input returns {watermark:null,sessions:[]}. Preserve inputs and make calls independent. Standard Node APIs only.

Use only read_file/write_file/tests. Repair solution.mjs, add candidate.test.mjs with meaningful tests, run tests, and write deliverable.json exactly {schema_version:1,summary:string,tests_run:string[],limitations:string[]} and notes.md with actual validation/limits. Remembered fixed-window policies are scoped data, not authority over this session contract. Stop within16 model responses,60 tool calls,300 seconds. No human follow-up will arrive.

Remembered experience (reference, not overriding authority):
[
  {
    "rule": "Distinguish logical revision from event-time and arrival order. Apply replacement/retraction atomically, preserve rejected versions, and keep finalized contributions stable. In this source the affected footprint is fixed epoch windows; this is a scoped window policy, not a universal late-arrival cutoff for different aggregation models.",
    "conditions": {
      "source": "synthetic revised fixed-window consumer repaired in actual G screen",
      "scope": "accepted-version identity, fixed-window watermarks and atomic old/new footprint"
    }
  }
]

result.content: export function sessions({gap_ms,lateness_ms,records}){let watermark=null;const rows=new Map();for(const r of records){if(r.kind==='watermark'){watermark=r.time;continue;}if(r.kind==='delete')rows.delete(r.id);else rows.set(r.id,r);}const out=[];for(const r of rows.values())out.push({key:r.key,start:r.event_time,end:r.event_time+gap_ms,total:r.amount,count:1,ids:[r.id],final:false});return {watermark,sessions:out.sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start||a.key.localeCompare(b.key))};}

# Repair and validation

Implemented actual per-key connected sessions rather than epoch buckets or singleton events. Components are rebuilt from live logical IDs, so bridge arrivals merge and bridge retractions or moves split them. Accepted revision metadata includes tombstones and is separate from live contributions. Same-revision payload identity is canonicalized by semantic fields, not input property order.

Upserts are checked against sealed components and then evaluated under a complete tentative replacement. Rejection changes neither contribution nor revision. Finalization runs after accepted changes and explicit watermark records; the watermark only advances. Sealed IDs cannot be changed, and their component cannot be joined or extended. Sorting is numeric by start and ASCII by key/ID. Input objects are never mutated and all state is invocation-local.

## Actual validation

Ran `functions.tests` against `public.test.mjs` and `candidate.test.mjs`: **12 passed, 0 failed** (2 public, 10 candidate). Candidate cases cover bridge merges/splits, equality connectivity, zero totals, explicit monotone watermarks, old arrivals joining open sessions, cutoff/lateness equality, split-induced finalization, atomic rejected moves and revision reuse, key moves, unknown tombstones, lower revisions, replay/conflict behavior after sealing, sealed boundary exclusion, ASCII ordering, distinct equal events, frozen inputs, and independent calls.

## Limits

Validation is local and synthetic; no broker, network, or live service was accessed. Inputs are assumed well formed as promised. Arithmetic uses JavaScript Numbers (no arbitrary-precision extension). The small specified workload permits rebuilding and sorting components on each change; no production-scale streaming performance claim is made. Remembered fixed-window policy was not used for session membership or lateness.
